entries.name: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam (PLE)
entries.publisher: Google Research with Mercor; expert-reviewed professional engineering tasks

development.score_scope: Public development split; request access and follow dataset terms. Use official dev leaderboard and exact dataset revision for comparisons.

hidden_test.score_scope: Do not request, copy, infer, or store hidden task data or graders. Scores only through the official competition route.

execution.repeat_policy: The published public development leaderboard reports model results averaged over three runs. The competition submission dev score is based on committed artifacts and a live harness check on a sample. The hidden competition leaderboard averages three harness runs. A Luminous matched dev comparison should use three independently identified full-set runs to align with the published dev baseline.

notes: The official site reports 48.3% for Claude Opus 5.5 on the 56-task hidden test set; the paper abstract separately reports a 50.6% strongest-configuration mean. These are distinct reported evaluation summaries and must not be compared as if they were the same split or run aggregation.

The Google Cloud / Mercor launch report (3 Nov 2026) reports 91% average individual-constraint satisfaction on co-authored tasks but only 41.3% of those deliverables passed every hard safety and feasibility check. This cohort scope must not be generalized to all 85 tasks.
The paper abstract reports an average of 27 million tokens and 63 minutes per task for its strongest configuration.
Do not use hidden-test scores as a baseline for a development-set result. Pin and compare against the official public development leaderboard on the same task revision.

The official competition page's 2026-11-04 snapshot also shows committed-artifact development scores (for example, Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Code 55.1% and GPT-6 Astra / Codex 53.0%). These are competition-entry artifact scores, not the three-run public development leaderboard mean described by the dataset card; do not compare them as the same evaluation mode.

leaderboard_snapshot.run_protocol: Each model is evaluated at highest reasoning effort in its native harness, three runs per task, isolated container without internet access, six-hour per-task limit.
leaderboard_snapshot.displayed_uncertainty_semantics: The official leaderboard displays a ± value for each score but the page does not define its statistical interpretation. Preserve it verbatim; do not label it a confidence interval, standard deviation, or standard error.
leaderboard_snapshot.comparability_warning: This hidden-test snapshot is not the public development leaderboard mean and is not the competition-entry development committed-artifact score. Do not compare these evaluation pathways as one baseline.

notes: This registry entry records metadata only. It does not define a second CEB task schema or receipt format.
Official PLE verifiers remain the scoring authority; CEB binds the Luminous harness/run provenance and external score artifacts.
No task execution is authorized until the isolation and evaluator-custody gates have been independently qualified.
The official dataset access gate must be satisfied through the authorized Hugging Face account. No access token belongs in source control or public logs.

PLE produces deliverables rather than source patches. Do not fabricate a patch digest or force PLE outputs into CEB v0's patch-centric receipt; use the canonical generic accounting/artifact mapping defined by #10314/#10370.

entries.paper_revision: Official blog snapshot 2026-10-12; published reference uses v2.0-core1; current v2.1 differs

development.score_scope: Public evaluation-only set; 100 cases across six tasks, disjoint from Core. Scores are for testing the harness and are explicitly not reportable.

hidden_test.score_scope: Core held-out 100-case set behind an evaluation-only agreement; published reference scores are calculated on this split. No task material is stored in this registry.

licensing.runner_code: Repository metadata does not declare a code license; verify with maintainers before redistribution or reuse.
licensing.development_dataset: BenchCAD 2.0 evaluation-only terms; public set terms prohibit training, fine-tuning, distillation, RL environments, pre-training/retrieval/search inclusion, redistribution and public posting of cases.

execution.runner_revision: v2.0-core1 for the published reference snapshot; v2.1 is a distinct non-comparable protocol
execution.repeat_policy: Published reference lines use harness v2.0: 30 rounds per case and reasoning is not carried between rounds. Claude rows are single repetitions; GPT-6 Astra is a mean of three repetitions except ECAD T6, which is one repetition. Current v2.1 carries reasoning across rounds and uses 60 rounds plus a 500,000 output-token budget per case; do not compare v2.1 scores with v2.0. Public-set scores are not reportable. Record exact per-model/per-task repetitions rather than assuming a uniform repeat count.

notes: The 2026-10-12 official blog reports GPT-6 Astra at max effort = 0.59 on the 100-case Core set, at about $11 per case, 135k tokens per case and 62 minutes median per case.
The same v2.0 snapshot reports Claude Opus 5.5 at max effort = 0.57, about $28 per case, 1.3M tokens per case and 3.7 hours per case.

The score is a mean across 100 Core cases with deterministic, non-LLM reference scoring. Parts are scored for geometry overlap and topology; assemblies additionally score placement; boards score wiring connectivity.

The blog reports that 83–96% of zero-scoring part types in evaluated assembly tasks had the right shape but wrong placement. At max effort, GPT-6 Astra found 80% of board connections and Claude Opus 5.5 68%; the blog describes serious rail shorts/splits and says the runs did not test for shorts or opens.
BenchCAD 2.0 scoring does not measure manufacturability or physical performance. Do not equate geometric/placement/connectivity score with engineering safety or production readiness.

Published v2.0 results and current v2.1 are different harness protocols. The current v2.1 protocol carries reasoning between rounds and allows 60 rounds / 500k output tokens per case; these are not comparable to v2.0.
Published 3-repetition mean except T6 ECAD, which has one repetition.
Published single repetition.

notes: Metadata only. No public or Core case has been downloaded or executed by Luminous.
Public and Core evaluation terms must be satisfied; held-out Core access requires the exact agreement.
Do not copy or expose BenchCAD public/Core cases, drawings, renders, reference artifacts or canaries in source control, retrieval or training corpora.
The benchmark emits CAD artifacts/assemblies or wiring graphs, not source patches. Use generic artifact accounting rather than CEB's patch-only DSSE subject.
